definition: Writing disorder is a type of learning disorder involving difficulties in written language. In DSM-5 it is grouped within the broader category of specific learning disorder rather than treated as a separate diagnosis, although some classification systems still regard it as a distinct type.

reasons: The packet supports that writing disorder is a type of learning disorder and that DSM-5 groups it within a single specific learning disorder category, with ICD-11 still treating LDs as discrete categories. However, it does not explicitly support the added claim that it involves difficulties in written language.

The packet does not explicitly state that “writing disorder… involve[s] difficulties in written language.” It only describes writing disorder as one of the types of specific learning disorders, without defining the nature of the writing-related difficulty in the text provided.

The DSM-5 part of the definition (“grouped within… specific learning disorder… rather than treated as a separate diagnosis”) is supported by the packet’s statement that DSM-5 integrates the various types (including writing disorder) into one single LD category.

The claim that “some classification systems still regard it as a distinct type” is broadly supported by the packet’s statement that ICD-11 adheres to discrete categories, but this does not repair the unsupported “difficulties in written language” wording.
